entries.text: | RST-02 | Zero-phase low-pass at 3.5 kHz | Band-limited input, low-band spectrum-copy extension |
| Bandwidth extension, 3.5 kHz cutoff | Band-limited input | 17.40 dB SI-SDR | Spectrum-copy extension falls to 14.39 dB |

- **RST-02:** the local copy-spectrum baseline should be rejected; it harms fidelity. The strongest ready-to-investigate neural family is bandwidth-conditioned generative upsampling, represented by NU-Wave 2, which targets different input rates and generates 48 kHz audio. Its authors provide official code and checkpoints, but those weights are not staged locally. High-frequency fidelity and content preservation need explicit evaluation because generated bands are estimates. [NU-Wave 2 paper](https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2022/han22_interspeech.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/maum-ai/nuwave2).

The registry divides this area into four different inverse problems: RST-01 declipping/saturation; RST-02 bandwidth extension; RST-03 codec-artifact restoration; and RST-04 packet-loss concealment. Their missing information and decoder context differ. A limiter cannot recover clipped peaks, resampling cannot infer missing high frequencies, and packet concealment benefits from codec state or redundant packets. A single “distortion restoration” score would hide these differences.
"plan_note": "Retain the negative comparison and require content preservation before inclusion.",
